name: EvolutionaryScale, PBC
subcategory: protein language / generative biology foundation models (ESM3, ESM C)
origin_detail: A public benefit company formed by the team that began building ESM protein language models at Meta's FAIR lab in 2019 (Alexander Rives, co-founder and chief scientist; with Tom Sercu and Sal Candido). They left after Meta disbanded the team and launched publicly on 25 Jun 2024 with ~20 staff. Its website now says 'EvolutionaryScale is now part of Biohub'.
openness_notes: At launch (Jun 2024) the 98B ESM3 was reachable only by API for non-commercial use, and the 1.4B ESM3-open weights and code came under the 'EvolutionaryScale Community License Agreement'. That licence was non-commercial only, barred commercial entities and use in drug discovery, and prohibited using outputs to train other models: level 1. As of Nov 2026 the ESM3 release page, the ESM C page and the GitHub repo (now under the Biohub org) say ESM3-open and all three ESM C sizes are open weights under the MIT licence. The largest ESM3 models stay API-only via the Biohub Platform under Biohub terms, so it is open core (level 2). The homepage sentence announcing MIT still links to the old community licence.

license_history.license: ESM3-open: EvolutionaryScale Community License Agreement (non-commercial, no drug discovery, no training other models); ESM3 98B via Forge API, non-commercial
ESM3-open and ESM C 300M/600M/6B under MIT; large ESM3 via Biohub Platform API
license_history.note: Current pages (Nov 2026). Date of relicensing not confirmed; appears tied to joining Biohub

relicensing_events.outcome_note: Relicensing coincides with the company becoming part of the non-profit Biohub (date not confirmed; before Aug 2026, when Biohub named Rives its Head of Science). A rare case of an AI-for-science startup opening its weights further after leaving the VC model.

exit_events.note: Company site: 'EvolutionaryScale is now part of Biohub'; models and APIs moved to biohub.ai under Biohub terms. Date, structure (acquisition vs merger or donation) and terms not found. Biohub listed Alex Rives as its Head of Science on 27 Aug 2026.

risk_events: Origin risk: the ESM team was disbanded at Meta (FAIR) before the spin-out
25 Jun 2024: $142M seed led by Nat Friedman, Daniel Gross and Lux Capital, with Amazon and NVentures
2025-2026 (date unconfirmed): ceased independent operation and became part of the non-profit Biohub; licences moved to MIT
robustness: As an independent VC-backed company it lasted roughly two years. The science and models now sit inside a philanthropically funded non-profit (Biohub), with weights for smaller models under MIT. That makes the models more robust to any single organization's fate (GitHub repo ~3.0k stars, ~408 forks) than they were under the non-commercial licence.
physical_science_relevance: Low to moderate. This is biology (proteins), not physical science. It matters to the study as an AI-for-science lab whose models were trained on public-scale protein sequence data: the homepage cites 2.78 billion natural proteins and 771 billion tokens, but fetched pages do not name the source databases. It started with restrictive weights and opened them after moving to a non-profit.
openness_effect_assessment: EvolutionaryScale launched with a restrictive, non-commercial 'community' licence designed to protect a VC business (API access to the 98B model). After it joined the non-profit Biohub, the smaller models moved to MIT. The open-weight releases (ESM3-open, ESM C) are what most researchers can actually use; commercial value was meant to come from the closed frontier model. The VC-funded API model did not persist as an independent company.
key_takeaway: EvolutionaryScale is the counter-example to 'start open, then close'. It began as a Meta FAIR open-science project (ESM), raised a $142M seed as a company with non-commercial open weights, and within about two years was folded into the non-profit Biohub, where its open models moved to MIT. For the study it suggests that frontier scientific foundation models may find a more stable home in philanthropic or non-profit structures than in VC-backed API businesses. Its timeline (relicence date, deal terms) still needs confirming.

verification_pass2.note: The MIT switch was not a single step from the 2024 Community License: LICENSE.md at v3.1.3 (2025-01-16) puts code under the 'Cambrian Open License Agreement' and ESM3-open weights under the 'Cambrian Non-Commercial License Agreement' (probably introduced with the 'esmc release' LICENSE.md commit of 2024-12-04, whose text was not opened); MIT replaced these on 2026-05-27. relicensing_events[0].from is therefore simplified; consider a Dec 2024/Jan 2025 license_history entry. The LICENSE copyright line ('Chan Zuckerberg Biohub, Inc.') settles that 'Biohub' is CZ Biohub. Free-text notes saying the relicence date is unconfirmed are now superseded. The repo's README history puts the Biohub rebranding between 2026-01-26 (README still linked github.com/evolutionaryscale) and 2026-05-27 (first 'Biohub Platform' commit, same day as the MIT switch); this dates the repo, not the corporate deal. Funding still rests on one journalism page, so confidence stays low.
